contents.name: 4.2 Restriction to Normal Subgroups
contents.support: Conjugation action and inertia; same left-action convention as this scaffold.

contents.name: Conjugate subrepresentations and their translates (unnumbered opening)
(4.2.1) Proposition
contents.support: For the assigned complex finite-group scope, apply published complete reducibility to N. The source proves a stronger arbitrary-field normal-restriction statement; no modular extension is needed here.

contents.name: Isotypical parts and inertia stability (paragraph preceding 4.2.2)
Restriction formula and ramification index (paragraph following 4.2.2)
contents.support: Module orbit and equal multiplicity carried by lem-normal-restriction-constituents-form-one-conjugacy-orbit; character formula by thm-clifford-homogeneous-restriction-formula.

contents.name: (4.4) and (4.5)
contents.support: Restriction of induction and its endomorphism dimension.

contents.name: (4.2.5) Remark
contents.support: Extension and quotient-tensor parametrization. Source has an unresolved cross-reference and a subgroup typo in its displayed induction; the scaffold proves the result by explicit multiplicity spaces.

contents.name: (4.2.6) Proposition
contents.reason: Extension of every character of an abelian normal subgroup in a split group is the extension-construction step of the next page, not required for an assumed extension in Gallagher.

contents.name: (4.2.7) Remark
contents.reason: Classification for split abelian normal subgroups is precisely the next page little-group method; ordinary Clifford and Gallagher here provide its prerequisites.

sources.title: Britta Späth, Reduction theorems for some global-local conjectures (November 27, 2017)
sources.locator: Notation p.1; §1 introductory action and full §1.A pp.2–3 through Remark 1.5; stop before §1.B

contents.name: 1. Clifford theory via projective representations (opening action and inertia)
contents.support: Right-conjugate source formula translated by replacing g with its inverse.

contents.name: Theorem 1.3 (Gallagher), extension definition and quotient case
contents.support: Definition of extension is carried by def-extension-of-an-irreducible-normal-subgroup-representation. Ordinary quotient correspondence only; proof supplied locally.

contents.name: Theorem 1.3, final generalized tensor-product clause
contents.reason: The character-triple tensor generalization is beyond the assigned quotient Gallagher result. As printed it reuses chi as an extension of theta while mapping Irr(G|theta) to Irr(G|tau theta), an inconsistent parameter choice; this clause is not used as a mathematical premise.

contents.name: Definition 1.4
contents.reason: Projective representations, similarity and irreducibility are definitions assigned to the next projective-extension page; ordinary linear extension theory here does not require them.

contents.name: 2-cocycles, 2-coboundaries and H2 (unnumbered after Definition 1.4)
contents.reason: The factor-set equivalence and obstruction class belong to the next page. Its cohomology-versus-homological-Schur-multiplier convention must be resolved there, not imported into ordinary Clifford theory.

contents.name: Remark 1.5 (More on projective representations), (a)
contents.reason: Rephasing a projective representation changes its factor set by a coboundary; this is needed for the next page obstruction class, not for an existing linear extension.

contents.name: Remark 1.5 (More on projective representations), (b)
contents.reason: Twisted group algebra modules encode a nontrivial factor set and are explicitly assigned to the next page; all algebras used here are ordinary group algebras.

item_support.locator: §4.2 opening pp.53–54; Späth notation p.1 and §1 opening p.2
item_support.support: For N normal in finite G and theta in Irr(N), use the existing left conjugate {}^g theta(n)=theta(g^{-1}ng). Define I=I_G(theta)={g: {}^g theta=theta}, and Irr(H|theta) for N<=H<=G by occurrence in restriction. The action factors through G/N and N<=I<=G.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For any complex G-module V and N normal in G, g V_theta=V_({}^g theta). Every N-submodule U of V decomposes as the direct sum of U intersect V_theta over the occurring N-types.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.locator: §4.2 p.54, Proposition 4.2.2 and following formula; Späth Theorem 1.1
item_support.support: For irreducible complex G-module V and any constituent theta of V|N, all constituents form the orbit of theta and all have the same positive multiplicity.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: If chi in Irr(G) lies over theta in Irr(N), I=I_G(theta), then Res_N^G chi=e sum_{gI in G/I} {}^g theta, e a positive integer. Hence chi(1)=e[G:I]theta(1). Use left cosets; the whole restriction need not be isotypical.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For chi lying over theta, its ramification index e(chi,theta) is the common multiplicity in the Clifford formula, equivalently dim Hom_N(S,V) for S affording theta.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For irreducible V and an occurring theta, the setwise stabilizer of V_theta in G equals I_G(theta). Thus V_theta is an I-module.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For irreducible V lying over theta, W=V_theta is irreducible over I=I_G(theta), and the canonical G-map Ind_I^G W -> V is an isomorphism.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: Let I=I_G(theta) and W in Irr(I|theta). Then W|N is theta-isotypical, Ind_I^G W is irreducible, and its theta-isotypical component is the identity-coset copy of W.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.locator: Theorem 1.2 p.2; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4(1–3,5) pp.55–56
item_support.support: Induction is a bijection Irr(I_G(theta)|theta) -> Irr(G|theta), with inverse taking the theta-isotypical component. Conjugate normal types give the same target set; the sets for distinct G-orbits partition Irr(G).
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For theta in Irr(N), Ind_N^G theta is irreducible iff I_G(theta)=N. Its character self-inner-product equals [I_G(theta):N].
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: For theta in Irr(N), let chi_j run over Irr(G|theta) and e_j=e(chi_j,theta). Then Ind_N^G theta=sum_j e_j chi_j and sum_j e_j^2=[I_G(theta):N].
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.locator: Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57
item_support.support: An extension of S in Irr(N) to H, N<=H<=G, is an H-action on S restricting to the given N-action; at character level Res_N^H chi_tilde=theta. It is automatically irreducible. Inflation from H/N is the published quotient construction.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.support: If S is irreducible over C and U is a finite theta-isotypical N-module, evaluation S tensor_C Hom_N(S,U) -> U, s tensor f -> f(s), is an N-isomorphism. Every N-submodule is S tensor M0 for a unique multiplicity subspace M0. N-maps between these modules correspond to linear maps between their multiplicity spaces.
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.locator: Theorem 1.3 p.2; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 p.57; Losev Corollary 2.16 and Proposition 2.17
item_support.support: Fix an extension S_tilde of theta to I=I_G(theta). Then eta -> chi_S_tilde Inf_(I/N)^I eta is a bijection Irr(I/N) -> Irr(I|theta). Composing with induction gives Irr(G|theta); the corresponding ramification index is eta(1).
item_support.qualification: Source-backed statement; detailed local proof planned in notes.

item_support.locator: §4.2 Theorem 4.2.4 / Proposition 4.2.3; Späth Theorem 1.3 specialized to S3
item_support.support: For A3=<r> in S3, Irr(A3)={1,lambda,lambda^{-1}}, lambda(r)=exp(2 pi i/3). Orbits {1} and {lambda,lambda^{-1}} have inertia S3 and A3. The trivial orbit gives trivial and sign; inducing lambda gives the standard degree-two irrep with ramification one.
item_support.qualification: Generated worked specialization, not claimed as a named source example.

item_support.locator: Theorem 1.3; tom Dieck Remark 4.2.5 specialized to a direct product
item_support.support: For finite N,Q and theta in Irr(N), inertia in N times Q is the full group. Extension S_tilde(n,q)=S(n) yields exactly S external-tensor U, U in Irr(Q), above theta, with ramification dim U.
item_support.qualification: Generated worked specialization, not claimed as a named source example.

item_support.locator: Theorems 1.1–1.3; tom Dieck Theorem 4.2.4 boundary specializations
item_support.support: For N=1, theta=1 and I=G; chi restricts to chi(1) copies of 1 and Clifford induction is identity. For N=G, theta=chi, I=G and e=1; the lying-over correspondence is the singleton identity.
item_support.qualification: Generated worked specialization, not claimed as a named source example.
